question: From which country were the ideals of justice of the Indian Constitution borrowed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The USSR**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct answer is **The USSR**__.
 
• The ideals of justice in the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the Constitution of the USSR.
 
• These ideals include social, economic, and political justice which aim to create a fair and equitable society.
 
• The concept of justice in the Indian Constitution is enshrined in the Preamble and forms a part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November 1949 and came into effect on 26th January 1950.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• The Preamble to the Constitution reflects the aspirations and objectives of the Constitution, including justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity.
 
• Justice in the Indian context is not limited to legal justice but also includes social and economic dimensions.
